plan_title: Oxy Hobbs Field CO2 Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The Hobbs Field boundary (North and South Hobbs Units), on the grounds that CO2 is already present throughout the field and kept there by fluid management; no buffer is added (p30-31).
mma_definition: The Hobbs Field plus a half-mile buffer (p31).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wellbores (about 700 field wells plus offset wells) and surface equipment are the pathways Oxy manages; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, new drilling and diffuse seal leakage are judged minimal or very unlikely (p4, p32-38).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The 'baselines' are the existing automated data systems: injection set points from pattern modeling, production forecasts, visual inspection work orders and H2S alarms, screened for possible CO2 leakage (p44-45).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHG reports by March 31, giving the mass balance and leak estimates; records kept at least three years. Well leaks are also reported to NMOCD and surface-facility leaks under Subpart W. No commitment to publish measurement data (p37-38, p45, p50, p52-53).

rows.detail: Custody transfer meters at the two Permian pipeline off-take points and the NHU-SHU transfer; operations meters at RCF inlets and outlets for produced and recycled CO2; composition sampled at least quarterly.
rows.location: Two custody transfer points, NHU-SHU transfer point, RCF inlets and outlets

rows.detail: Injection rate and pressure targets from pattern modeling programmed into WAG satellite controllers; pressure monitors flag deviations; data sent to a central monitoring station; automatic shutoff if pressure exceeds fracture pressure.
rows.location: Each injection well, via WAG headers at satellites
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside set points: automatic flag, field investigation, work order if not readily resolved; screened for possible CO2 leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Well pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Annular pressure at wellheads monitored for tubing leaks; state rules also require Bradenhead gauges to measure pressure between casing strings.
rows.trigger_or_response: Annulus anomaly: inspect; simple repairs made on the spot, otherwise work order; workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: NMOCD MITs on all active injectors before injection, every two years, after workovers or casing repairs; casing-tubing annulus tested to 300 psi for 30 minutes.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: well shut in immediately, NMOCD notified, casing repaired and retested or well plugged.
rows.evidence_quote: Every 2 years as stated in the injection orders (NMOCD Order NO. R-4934-F / R-6199-F);

rows.detail: Each producer diverted to satellite test equipment for 8-12 hours about every two months; produced gas sampled quarterly, oil sampled yearly for CO2; results compared with forecast.
rows.location: Each production well; satellite batteries; RCF inlets
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management personnel investigate; work order if not resolved quickly.
rows.evidence_quote: There is a routine cycle for each satellite battery, with each well being tested approximately once every two months.

rows.detail: Plan says injection-zone pressure is monitored continually and automatically, and IWR kept near 1.0; the response table says this is read at WAG headers and in new wells, not observation wells.
rows.location: Injection zone, read at WAG headers and new wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained pressure or high pressure in new wells: investigate; responses include resealing abandoned wells and shutting in injectors near faults or seismic events.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy monitors wells through continual, automated pressure monitoring in the injection zone

rows.detail: Two-part visual inspection by about 40 field staff: routine facility visits checking equipment, valves and WAG schedules, watching for white CO2 clouds, ice and fluid leaks; also watches for unapproved drilling.
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak or problem found: repair on the spot or work order; critical leaks acted on immediately; leak quantified for annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors at all times (detection limit 10 ppm); H2S treated as a proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.location: Worn by field personnel (about 40 on site)
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, quantify CO2 leak; MRV lead notified of confirmed H2S incidents.
rows.evidence_quote: all field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors at all times

rows.detail: Under Oxy's voluntary SFRM program, wells and equipment screened as near the public get H2S sensors and gas-triggered automatic shut-off valves; plan does not say how many locations qualify.
rows.location: SFRM-screened wells and surface equipment near the City of Hobbs
rows.trigger_or_response: Triggered safeguards are investigated to determine whether CO2 leaked.
rows.evidence_quote: SFRM guidelines call for using enhanced materials for well heads, installing sensors to detect H2S

rows.detail: Cement bond logs and temperature surveys were used historically to find top of cement on 1946-1979 wells; CBLs are listed among corrosion-protection procedures. Not part of MRV monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: Cement bond logs (CBL) or temperature surveys (TS) have been used to determine that this depth is available on most wells.

rows.detail: One-time review of recorded Permian Basin earthquakes (literature including Frohlich 2012); none in the field, closest about 80 miles away. No seismic monitoring committed.
rows.trigger_or_response: Response table lists shutting in injectors near a seismic event.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy has reviewed the nature and location of seismic events within the vicinity of the Hobbs Field.

rows.detail: Seismic surveys from field development cited as showing deep faults that do not reach the San Andres; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: seismic surveys have been conducted to characterize the formations and provide information for the reservoir models

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors for equipment leaks and vents, plus event-driven quantification of leaks found through work orders, reconciled to avoid double counting.
rows.location: Surface equipment between meters and wellheads
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy uses 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W to estimate surface leaks from equipment at the Hobbs Field.

rows.detail: Step-rate tests measure formation fracture pressure so injection pressure can be held below it.
rows.evidence_quote: keeping injection pressure below the formation fracture pressure, which is measured using step-rate

notes: Well-test frequency is inconsistent: about every two months (p24, p33) but 'once during each monthly cycle' on p41; coded periodic_unspecified. 'Reservoir pressure' is read at WAG headers and in new wells (Table 3, p37-38); no observation wells or bottom-hole gauges are named. Fixed H2S sensors exist only where the voluntary SFRM program applies; coverage not stated. The 'two-part' visual inspection never clearly defines the second part. AMA has no buffer; the MMA adds the half mile. Older-style plan (2017): no seismic, soil gas, groundwater or atmospheric monitoring.
